gp.text: (5) Gross profit for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 includes inventory losses of $95 million from the Incheon FC Fire. Net loss for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 includes a loss of $180 million related to the Incheon FC Fire, net of taxes.

cor.heading: Cost of Sales
cor.text:
Cost of sales primarily consists of the purchase price of products sold directly to customers where we record revenue gross, and includes logistics costs. Inbound shipping and handling costs to receive products from suppliers are included in inventory and recognized in cost of sales as products are sold. Additionally, cost of sales includes outbound shipping and logistics-related expenses, delivery costs from our restaurant delivery business, and depreciation and amortization expense.

Cost of sales increased mainly due to higher volume from increased sales and customer demand and the $95 million Product Commerce inventory loss from the Incheon FC Fire. Cost of sales as a percentage of revenue increased primarily due to an increase for Product Commerce from 67.9% and 68.0% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025 to 71.6% and 70.3% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily from the impact of the Incident, including increased costs in supply chain management and a higher rate of customer discounts. In addition, the inventory losses from the Incheon FC Fire increased Product Commerce cost of sales as a percentage of revenue by approximately 1.1% and 0.4% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively.

costs.text: (1) Administrative fines include only certain significant regulatory fines and penalties that Coupang does not consider to be normal operating expenses related to the Company’s ongoing operations, revenue generating activities, business strategy, industry, and regulatory environment, as discussed in Note 10 — “Commitments and Contingencies” .

ga.heading: Operating, General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text:
Operating, general and administrative expenses include all our operating costs excluding cost of sales, as described above. More specifically, these expenses include costs incurred in operating and staffing our fulfillment centers (including costs attributed to receiving, inspecting, picking, packaging, and preparing customer orders), customer service-related costs, payment processing fees, costs related to the design, execution, and maintenance of our technology infrastructure and online offerings, advertising costs, general corporate function costs, and depreciation and amortization expense.

The increase in operating, general and administrative expenses for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 primarily reflects increases in fulfillment, technology, and marketing costs to support our continued growth, as well as $153 million of losses related to the Incheon FC Fire, including fixed asset impairment losses and other directly-related losses. The increase for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 also reflects the impact of certain administrative fines of approximately $410 million. The Incheon FC Fire losses increased operating, general and administrative expenses as a percentage of revenue by 1.5% and 0.6% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively.

da_op.text: Segment Adjusted EBITDA is defined as income (loss) before income taxes for a period before depreciation and amortization, equity-based compensation expense, interest expense, interest income, and other income (expense), net. Segment adjusted EBITDA also excludes impairments and other items that we do not believe are reflective of our ongoing operations.

nonint.text: (1) Administrative fines include only certain significant regulatory fines and penalties that Coupang does not consider to be normal operating expenses related to the Company’s ongoing operations, revenue generating activities, business strategy, industry, and regulatory environment, as discussed in Note 10 — “Commitments and Contingencies” .

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text:
Interest expense primarily consists of interest on our short-term borrowings and long-term debt.

Interest expense remained flat compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 and decreased $10 million compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively, due to the interest expense in the prior year periods associated with the Farfetch syndicated term loans that were redeemed in July 2025.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Our tax provision for income taxes for interim periods is determined using an estimate of our annual effective tax rate, adjusted for discrete items, if any, that are taken into account in the relevant period. Each quarter we update our estimate of the annual effective tax rate, and if our estimated tax rate changes, we make a cumulative adjustment. No income tax benefit was accrued for certain jurisdictions where we anticipate incurring a loss during the full fiscal year as the related deferred tax assets were fully offset by a valuation allowance. Our resulting effective tax rate differs from the applicable statutory rate, primarily due to tax credits, U.S. taxes on foreign earnings such as the inclusion of the NCTI provisions, the valuation allowance against deferred tax assets in loss making jurisdictions, and other permanent differences.

Our tax provision for income taxes for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was unfavorably impacted by losses before income taxes in certain jurisdictions for which we receive no tax benefit, resulting in a negative effective tax rate for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

net.text: (4) Net loss for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 includes certain administrative fines of approximately $410 million.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: The year-over-year change in operating cash flow was driven by a $1.6 billion decrease to net (loss) income, including $410 million for certain administrative fines that remained unpaid as of September 30, 2026, and $248 million of losses resulting from the Incheon FC Fire. Cash provided by operating activities was also impacted by $461 million of cash payments for income taxes. In addition, changes in working capital included a $264 million decrease in inventory, primarily reflecting the timing of inventory purchases.

net sales.heading: Total Net Revenues
net sales.text:
We categorize our total net revenues as (1) net retail sales and (2) net other revenue. Total net revenues incorporate reductions for estimated returns, promotional discounts, and earned loyalty rewards and exclude amounts collected on behalf of third parties, such as value added taxes. We periodically provide customers with promotional discounts to retail prices, such as percentage discounts and other similar offers, to incentivize increased customer spending and loyalty. These promotional discounts are discretionary and are reflected as reductions to the selling price and revenue recognized on each corresponding transaction. Loyalty rewards are offered as part of revenue transactions to all retail customers, whereby rewards are earned as a percentage of each purchase, for the customer to apply towards the purchase price of a future transaction. We defer a portion of revenue from each originating transaction, based on the estimated standalone selling price of the loyalty reward earned, and then recognize the revenue as the loyalty reward is redeemed in a future transaction, or when the reward expires. The amount of the deferred revenue related to these loyalty rewards is not material.

It operates in over 190 countries and territories around the world.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt (incl. current portion)
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans, current maturities included: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Cash and equivalents
accounts.note: The cash flow statement's cash can include restricted cash the balance sheet shows elsewhere: a small residual is that difference.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

We rely on a combination of patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, license agreements, confidentiality procedures, non-disclosure agreements, employee non-disclosure and invention assignment agreements, and other legal and contractual rights to establish and protect our intellectual property and proprietary rights.
• we rely on Pay to conduct a substantial amount of the payment processing across our business.
As such, you should not rely on our business and financial performance in any prior quarterly or annual period as an indication of our future business or financial performance.

We rely on encryption and authentication technology in an effort to securely transmit and store data about our customers, merchants, suppliers, advertisers, and others, including personally identifiable information, as well as other confidential and proprietary information but such measures cannot provide absolute security and may fail to operate as intended or be circumvented.
Our future business and financial performance depends on continued demand for the types of goods and services that we and our merchants offer.
Our revenue depends on prompt and accurate payment processes.

Because our decision to raise additional capital will depend on numerous considerations, including factors beyond our control, we cannot predict or estimate the amount, timing, or nature of any future debt or equity financings, or terms on which any such financings may be completed.

Our financial performance depends on our ability to identify, originate, and define retail trends, as well as to anticipate, gauge, and react to changing customer preferences in a timely manner, including seasonal trends in customer spending.

We depend on our ability to attract and retain merchants that offer high-quality merchandise and services to our customers at attractive prices and in a timely manner to attract new customers and to keep our existing customers engaged and purchasing from our apps and websites.
Our business depends on the continued growth of online commerce and the increased acceptance of online transactions by potential customers.

For more information, see the risk factor below titled “ Our business depends on network and mobile infrastructure, third-party data center hosting facilities, other third-party providers, and our ability to maintain and scale our technology.
Growth in our advertising revenue depends on our ability to continue to develop and offer advertisers effective tools and promotions.
We rely on Pay to conduct a substantial amount of the payment processing across our businesses in Korea.
We rely on the convenience and ease of use that Pay provides to our customers and merchants.
We rely on our merchants to provide a high-quality experience to our customers.
Our business depends on network and mobile infrastructure, third-party data center hosting facilities, other third-party providers, and our ability to maintain and scale our technology.
We depend on the development and maintenance of the Internet and mobile infrastructure.

We rely on the Internet to communicate with our customers and merchants and, accordingly, depend on the continuous, reliable, and secure operation of Internet servers, related hardware and software, and network infrastructure.

Our operations depend on protecting the virtual cloud infrastructure hosted in AWS and its configuration, architecture, and interconnection specifications, as well as the information stored in these virtual data centers and which third-party Internet service providers transmit.

We also rely on e-mail service providers, bandwidth providers, Internet service providers, and mobile networks to deliver e-mail and “push” communications to customers and to allow customers to access our apps and websites.
Our revenue depends on the number of customers who shop on our apps and websites and the volume of orders that we can handle.

Our future performance may depend on Korea’s future economic growth.

Our use of open source software may also present additional security risks because the source code for open source software is publicly available, which may make it easier for hackers and other third parties to determine how to breach our apps or websites and systems that rely on open source software.

Realization of these NOL carryforwards depends on our future taxable income in the taxing jurisdiction and there is a risk that portions of our existing carryforwards could expire unused or otherwise be unavailable to offset future income tax liabilities, which could materially and adversely affect our operating results.
